context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides self-service portals and circulation management for academic and public libraries. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Students, Public Citizens)
* Librarians / Circulation Staff
* Library Administrators
* Library Management System
* Catalogue Database (Transactional & Read Replica)
* External Institutional BI Tools / Municipal Dashboards

## Relationships
* Library Patrons to Library Management System via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
* Librarians/Administrators to Library Management System via OAuth2/OIDC with MFA
* Library Management System to Catalogue Database via AES-256 encrypted connections
* Library Management System to External BI Tools via mTLS API push with pseudonymized data

## Technology Stack
* TLS 1.3: Enforces secure external traffic encryption
* AES-256: Secures data at rest for the catalogue database and read replica
* OAuth2/OIDC: Manages token-based federation and authentication for staff
* Read Replica: Isolates heavy analytical queries to protect transactional performance

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR compliance and EU data residency while protecting the critical R-05 search performance requirement through read replicas and strict trust boundaries.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons, Librarians, and Library Administrators
* API Gateway
* Self-Service Portal Container
* Circulation Management Container
* Analytics/Reporting Container
* Catalogue Database and Read-Replica Data Store
* External Institutional BI Tools and Municipal Dashboards
* Message Broker (Kafka / RabbitMQ)

## Relationships
* Patrons and Staff interact with the API Gateway via HTTPS using OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs
* Inter-container communication uses mTLS via Istio service mesh
* Core containers query the Catalogue Database and read-replica store via TLS 1.3
* Core containers publish events asynchronously to the Message Broker for the Analytics Container
* Analytics Container provides aggregated data to Library Administrators

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: EU-region-only managed clusters for data residency compliance
* Istio: Service mesh for mTLS and trust boundaries
* OAuth2/OIDC & JWT: Authentication and RBAC at the API Gateway
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing to maintain <800ms search latency
* Kafka / RabbitMQ: Asynchronous event ingestion for analytics
* AES-256 & TLS 1.3: Data encryption at rest and in transit

## Rationale
This architecture enforces EU data residency through regional deployments and strict egress controls. It guarantees sub-800ms search performance via independent stateless services, read-replicas, and asynchronous telemetry.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries designed to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and maintains a 99th-percentile search response time under 800 ms.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons, Librarians / Circulation Staff, Library Administrators
* API Gateway (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT, Redis)
* Self-Service Portal Container (Kubernetes, Istio)
* Circulation Management Container (Kubernetes, Istio)
* Analytics/Reporting Container (Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana)
* Catalogue Database, Message Broker (Kafka / RabbitMQ)

## Relationships
* Library Patrons -> API Gateway: Accesses self-service portals [HTTPS via OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs]
* Librarians -> API Gateway: Interacts with circulation management [HTTPS via OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs]
* Library Administrators -> API Gateway: Interacts with system administration and analytics [HTTPS via OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs]
* API Gateway -> Self-Service Portal Container: Routes requests [mTLS via Istio]
* API Gateway -> Circulation Management Container: Routes requests [mTLS via Istio]

## Technology Stack
* API Gateway: Entry point utilizing OAuth2/OIDC, JWT validation, Redis caching, and WAF for perimeter security.
* Kubernetes & Istio: Orchestration and service mesh providing mTLS, circuit breaking, and traffic shifting.
* OpenTelemetry & Prometheus/Grafana: Observability stack for real-time latency monitoring and HPA scaling.
* Anycast DNS: Geo-routing technology to enforce EU data residency and minimize TLS handshake latency.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures secure, isolated access for diverse user personas while meeting stringent performance requirements through edge routing and service mesh optimization. Furthermore, it guarantees compliance with EU-only data residency constraints and high availability via stateless scalability.

Self-Service Portal Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a digital solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items and manage circulation. The Self-Service Portal Container specifically delivers patron-facing discovery and autonomous account workflows.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Primary Users)
* Self-Service Portal Container (Kubernetes, Istio)
* API Gateway (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT)
* Catalogue Database and Read-Replica Data Store
* Distributed Cache (Redis)
* Content Delivery Network (CDN)

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Self-Service Portal Container: Routes requests [mTLS via Istio]
* Self-Service Portal Container -> Distributed Cache (Redis): Offloads frequent catalogue queries [In-cluster]
* Self-Service Portal Container -> Read-Replica Data Store: Queries catalogue data [TLS 1.3]
* Self-Service Portal Container -> CDN: Delivers localized static assets [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes & Istio: Container orchestration and service mesh for zero-downtime canary deployments and mTLS.
* Redis: Distributed caching layer to guarantee 99th-percentile search response times under 800 ms.
* OpenTelemetry: End-to-end tracing with PII scrubbing for EU GDPR compliance.
* Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA): Dynamic scaling based on CPU and request latency.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency and meets sub-800ms search performance SLAs through targeted caching and auto-scaling. Robust security controls, including short-lived JWTs and input validation, protect patron privacy.

Circulation Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Circulation Management Container is a core backend service within the Library Management System that executes check-outs, returns, renewals, and loan policy enforcement. It ensures high-performance, secure, and EU-compliant library operations for patrons and staff.

## Key Elements
* **Circulation Management Container**: Kubernetes-hosted microservice handling circulation logic.
* **API Gateway**: Entry point issuing OAuth2/OIDC JWTs and routing external traffic.
* **Catalogue Database & Read-Replica**: Multi-zone replicated data store for items and loans.
* **Message Broker**: Kafka / RabbitMQ for asynchronous event publishing.
* **Cloud KMS / Vault**: Secret management and encryption key provider.

## Relationships
* **API Gateway -> Circulation Management Container**: Routes validated requests via Istio mTLS.
* **Circulation Management Container -> Catalogue Database**: Executes queries and updates using TLS 1.3 with connection pooling and circuit-breaking.
* **Circulation Management Container -> Message Broker**: Publishes asynchronous domain events over TLS 1.3.

## Technology Stack
* **Kubernetes & Istio**: Container orchestration and service mesh ensuring mTLS, circuit-breaking, and EU node pinning.
* **OpenTelemetry & Prometheus**: Distributed tracing and metrics for monitoring transaction latencies (<500ms SLA).
* **AES-256 & Kubernetes Secrets**: Data-at-rest encryption and dynamic credential injection via Vault.
* **Idempotent REST APIs**: Ensures safe request retries without local state persistence.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict compliance with EU data residency laws by pinning workloads and encrypting PII at rest. It prioritizes operational resilience through multi-zone database replication, API idempotency, and Istio circuit-breaking to protect physical library workflows.

Analytics/Reporting Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It utilizes the Analytics/Reporting Container to process asynchronous events and deliver aggregated administrative reporting under strict EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
* Library Administrators
* Analytics/Reporting Container (Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry)
* Dedicated OLAP Data Store (ClickHouse / PostgreSQL read-replica)
* Message Broker (Kafka / RabbitMQ)
* External Institutional BI Tools and Municipal Dashboards

## Relationships
* Message Broker -> Analytics/Reporting Container: Streams analytics events [Kafka / RabbitMQ protocol over TLS 1.3]
* Analytics/Reporting Container -> External Institutional BI Tools and Municipal Dashboards: Exports aggregated data, reports, and webhooks [HTTPS / TLS 1.3, mTLS, HMAC-SHA256]
* Library Administrators -> Analytics/Reporting Container: Accesses customized dashboards and scheduled reports [HTTPS, JWT-based RBAC]

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes & Istio: Container orchestration, service mesh egress validation, and SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing, custom HPA metrics, and immutable audit logging
* ClickHouse / PostgreSQL: Dedicated read-optimized OLAP storage for batch workload isolation
* AES-256 & TLS 1.3: Data-at-rest encryption and secure transport protocols

## Rationale
This architecture isolates heavy batch reporting workflows to protect real-time search performance and satisfy sub-800ms latency goals. It enforces EU data residency and GDPR compliance through automated geo-checks, data masking, and secure egress policies.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a Library Management System designed to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals.]
[It uses a secure, event-driven architecture to deliver real-time operational insights while strictly enforcing EU data residency constraints.]

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons, Librarians / Circulation Staff, Library Administrators
* Catalogue Database, External Institutional BI Tools / Municipal Dashboards
* API Gateway (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT)
* Self-Service Portal Container & Circulation Management Container (Kubernetes, Istio)
* Analytics/Reporting Container (Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry)
* Message Broker (Kafka / RabbitMQ, Strimzi operator)
* Schema Registry (Confluent Schema Registry)
* Secret Management (HashiCorp Vault / Kubernetes Secrets Store CSI driver)

## Relationships
* Circulation Management Container -> Message Broker: Publishes events asynchronously [Kafka/RabbitMQ protocol over TLS 1.3 with mTLS & SCRAM-SHA-512]
* Message Broker -> Analytics/Reporting Container: Streams events for analytics [Kafka/RabbitMQ protocol over TLS 1.3]
* Message Broker -> Dead Letter Queue (DLQ): Routes malformed/unprocessable events securely

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes & Istio: Container orchestration and internal mesh traffic isolation
* Kafka / RabbitMQ (Strimzi): Managed asynchronous event streaming with 3-broker cluster and replication factor of 2
* TLS 1.3 & AES-256: Transport encryption and EU-resident persistent volume encryption
* Confluent Schema Registry: Event schema governance to prevent breaking changes
* HashiCorp Vault: Dynamic mTLS certificate rotation and credential management
* OpenTelemetry: End-to-end event latency tracking and consumer lag monitoring

## Rationale
[This architecture fits requirements by decoupling asynchronous event streaming from core circulation tasks, protecting search performance well under the 800ms NFR.]
[It strictly enforces EU data residency, GDPR pseudonymization, and transport-level security to satisfy compliance mandates while delivering real-time analytics.]
Message Broker.yaml_definition:
level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Message Broker container"
parentContainer:
  name: "Message Broker"
elements:
  - type: "component"
    name: "Event Ingestion Engine"
    technology: "Kafka / RabbitMQ, Strimzi operator"
    description: "Handles incoming asynchronous events from the Circulation Management Container using TLS 1.3 and mTLS & SCRAM-SHA-512."
  - type: "component"
